summary: The pretrained GRASP-A2 model at Layer 6 encodes significantly more explicit chemical structure than random initialization or reference models, despite receiving bond-type inputs that make some features redundant.

claims.claim: Pretrained A2 learns ~1.9x more context-chemistry latents than the T08b Reference GRASP model.
claims.evidence: A2 has 178 'context_chemistry' latents compared to Ref's ~93 (T08b ref) and Random's 11.
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `[#6]` vs `[n]`. Prediction: Latent count should drop if trained on non-aromatic dataset.
claims.prediction: If true, training A2 on a saturated alkane-only set will reduce 'bond_derived' and 'functional_group' counts significantly below 178.

claims.claim: Explicit bond inputs do not eliminate internal encoding of hybridization/aromaticity at Layer 6.
claims.evidence: 'bond_derived' family contains 84 latents (highest count). Top latent 170 fires on C with 'hybridization_SP', AUROC=1.0, n_fire=325.
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `[C;H3]` vs `[#6X4]`. Prediction: Latent 170 should fire selectively on sp3 carbons regardless of input token type.
claims.prediction: If true, filtering atoms to only those with RDKit property 'hybridization' == 'SP2' will zero out activation for latent 170 (AUROC drops).

claims.claim: Functional group detection is robust and distinct from simple neighbor counts.
claims.evidence: 'functional_group' family has 50 latents. Top examples include `fg_ether` (latent 1182, AUROC=0.984) and `fg_nitrile` (latent 357/459, AUROC=1.0).
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `[C]-[O]-[C]` vs `[#6X2]=[N+]`. Prediction: Latents for ether/nitrile should not fire on esters or nitro groups.
claims.prediction: If true, applying a filter to exclude ethers from the dataset will reduce activation of latent 1182 by >90%.

claims.claim: Random initialization fails to capture chemical structure despite identical inputs and architecture.
claims.evidence: Random A2 has only 11 'context_chemistry' latents vs 178 for pretrained. Dead fraction is high (523/4096 dead).
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `[#6]`. Prediction: Latent counts should remain low (<20) across multiple random seeds.
claims.prediction: If true, repeating the SAE training on 10 different random weight initializations will yield a mean 'context_chemistry' count <30.

claims.claim: The model encodes ring size context specifically for small rings (strain).
claims.evidence: 'ring' family has 23 latents. Top examples include `min_ring_size_4` (latent 1943, AUROC=0.98) and `min_ring_size_3` (latent 122, AUROC=0.975).
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `[C]1CC1`. Prediction: Latents should fire on cyclopropane/cyclobutane motifs.
claims.prediction: If true, removing all rings < 6 atoms from the dataset will reduce 'ring' family count to near zero.

claims.claim: Neighbor information is encoded as a distinct chemical feature class.
claims.evidence: 'neighbour' family has 21 latents. Top example `has_O_neighbor` (latent 357, AUROC=0.98).
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `[C]-[O]`. Prediction: Latent should fire on alcohols/ethers but not pure hydrocarbons.
claims.prediction: If true, filtering for molecules with no heteroatoms will reduce 'neighbour' family activation to near zero.

trivial_explanations: Hybridization and aromaticity are explicitly provided in A2 inputs; the model may be redundantly encoding them at Layer 6 rather than inferring them.
The high FVU (0.145) for A2 compared to Ref GRASP (0.075) suggests Layer 6 activations contain more variance/noise, requiring more latents to explain.
